name: Shoal of Small Lights
description: A sphere that exists only as a shoal of fine teal points, crowding into a bright rim where the surface turns away from us; it wakes sparse and low, fills out and rises by noon, drifts across in the evening, and thins to a lone glowing ring at night, while each hour of the day's music is laid down as one brightened latitude band on its turning skin.
listening: Bass breath gently swells the sphere, rising tension tightens and lifts its rim halo, the key tilts the axis and leans the points between aqua and pale mint, treble sharpens each point, every song re-scatters the constellation, and iDay turns the music of each hour into a denser, brighter band of latitude so the globe becomes a portrait of the day by midnight.

curator.verdict: It follows the teal dot sphere direction closely, with a bright rim, dark ground and calm space, and it looks nothing like the recent warm-glow days. But the hundreds of fine, evenly scattered high-contrast points will sparkle and shimmer on a 64x64 grid, and the four stills barely differ beyond size and position, so the day's arc is weak.
